## Lecture Overview

- Effect Size
- Effect Detection
- Moderators
- Mediators
- Meta-Analysis

## Effect Size {.smaller}

- **Magnitude**: how large an effect is
- **Effect size**: a ***standardized*** measure of effect magnitude
  - Can be compared across outcomes in different units / scales
- **Standardized mean difference**: program effect in ***standard deviation units***
  - Most common type of effect size measure
  - ***Cohen's D*** & ***Hedges' G*** are most common standardized mean diff statistics
- Rules of thumb for education field research[^fn-kraft]:
  - \> .20 = large
  - .05--.20 = medium
  - < .05 = small
- ...but everything is context-specific!

[^fn-kraft]: Kraft, M. A. (2020). Interpreting Effect Sizes of Education Interventions. *Educational Researcher*. [https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3102/0013189X20912798](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3102/0013189X20912798)

## Effect Estimates Contain "Noise" {#noise}

- **Noise**: non-systematic error; [see appendix for demonstration](#noise-demo)
  - (bias = systematic error)
- Is our effect estimate real, or is it just noise?
  - We need a ***large enough effect estimate*** that we can be ***confident it's coming from a real effect*** and not just noise
  - "signal-to-noise ratio"

## Statistical Significance & Power {.smaller}

- **Statistical significance**: formalized procedure for ***evaluating likelihood that effect estimates are "real"*** and not just noise
  - If this procedure determines that the effect is "statistically significant," we feel confident that it's real
- **Statistical power**: how ***likely we are*** to find statistical significance, aka ***detect the effect***
- Power is based on factors including:
  - Effect size
  - Sample size
  - Variation in outcome
- We can ***increase power by reducing noise*** (aka increasing **precision**)
  - Increase sample size
  - Adjust for baseline covariates (to reduce outcome variation)

## Minimum Detectable Effect Size

- **Minimum detectable effect size (MDES)**: the ***smallest effect you are likely to detect*** given your power & precision
- The ***larger the sample***, the ***smaller your MDES*** will be
  - But, the ***more costly*** your study will be (if collecting data)
- **Practical significance**: an effect size that would represent a ***meaningful change*** in outcomes
  - No need to try to detect an effect any smaller than that

## Moderators: Effect Variation

- Effects may be different for different subgroups of program participants
- **Moderator**: a variable that defines subgroups for whom program effects differ
  - E.g. demographics, SES, pre-program outcome levels, etc.
- **Dosage** analysis: moderator analysis that examines if effects differ for people who received different amounts of program services
- **Implementation fidelity** can be a moderator; shows if effects varied when prog components were implemented with more fidelity

## Mediator: Effect Pathways

- **Mediator**: a proximal outcome that affects a more distal outcome
- Sometimes called a "***mechanism***" that explains ***how the program affects the main outcome*** of interest

```{dot}
//| fig-height: 1.5
//| fig-width: 7
digraph G {
  graph [rankdir=LR ranksep=0.45]
  node [shape=box fontname="../../../../../Roboto-Regular" fontsize=14 margin="0.16,0.10"]
  prog [label=<Program>]
  mediator [label=<Mediator>]
  outcome [label=<Main Outcome>]

  edge [arrowsize=0.5]
  prog -> mediator -> outcome
}
```

- Can test for mediation by:
  - Estimating effects of prog on mediator & on the more distal outcome
  - See if there's a relationship between change in the mediator and change in the distal outcome

## Meta-Analysis {.parens}

- **Meta-analysis**: statistical synthesis of all evaluations on a certain program type, outcome, or other specified criteria
- Step 1: systematically gather all published evaluations that meet criteria
- Step 2: statistically combine effect sizes to get the average effect size & variance
- Used to: 
  (a) inform future evaluations
  (b) contribute to general knowledge about programs

# Appendix

## Noise From <br>Randomization & Sampling Error {#noise-demo}

[back to main slide](#noise){style="font-size: 0.6em;"}

```{r}
set.seed(6)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
# starting sample; the sample size buttons below redraw at other sizes
n <- 100
data <- data.frame(
  participate = rep(c(1,0), each = n / 2)
) |>
  mutate(
    group = ifelse(participate == 1, 'participant', 'comparison'),
    # drawn the same way for both groups, as if randomly assigned
    test_score = rnorm(n, 100, 25),
    income = rnorm(n, 75, 25),
    age = rnorm(n, 12, 2),
    prek = rbinom(n, 1, .45),
    y0 = test_score + income * .1 + age * 2 + prek * 5
  )

# hand the data to the interactive pieces below (Observable JS)
ojs_define(ra_data = data)
```

::: {.ra}
```{ojs}
// blur so the arrow keys / space keep moving the slides after a click
ra_blur = () => document.activeElement?.blur()

// starts at R's sample size
viewof ra_n = {
  const input = Inputs.radio([100, 1000, 10000], {
    label: "Sample size",
    value: ra_data.participate.length,
    format: n => n.toLocaleString()
  })
  input.addEventListener("input", ra_blur)
  return input
}
```

<!-- buttons in one row (styles in style_9.css) -->
::: {.ra-buttons}
```{ojs}
// a new sample of n people, drawn like the R chunk above (keep the two in
// sync): first half participants, second half comparison
ra_resample = n => d3.range(n).map(i => {
  const draw = (mean, sd) => d3.randomNormal(mean, sd)()
  const participate = i < n / 2 ? 1 : 0
  const test_score = draw(100, 25)
  const income = draw(75, 25)
  const age = draw(12, 2)
  const prek = d3.randomBernoulli(.45)()
  const y0 = test_score + income * .1 + age * 2 + prek * 5
  return {participate, group: participate === 1 ? "participant" : "comparison",
    test_score, income, age, prek, y0}
})

// R's sample at its own size, and a new draw at the others
ra_start = ra_n === ra_data.participate.length ? transpose(ra_data) : ra_resample(ra_n)

// Re-randomize shuffles who participates (still half per group);
// Re-sample redraws the data and keeps the current assignment. both start
// over when the sample size changes
viewof ra_state = Inputs.button([
  ["re-randomize", s => { ra_blur(); return {...s, assign: d3.shuffle(s.assign.slice())} }],
  ["re-sample", s => { ra_blur(); return {...s, rows: ra_resample(ra_n)} }]
], {value: {assign: ra_start.map(d => d.participate), rows: ra_start}})

ra_assign = ra_state.assign
ra_rows = ra_state.rows
```

```{ojs}
viewof ra_show_full = Inputs.button("full data", {value: false, reduce: v => { ra_blur(); return !v }})
```
:::

```{ojs}
// data with the current assignment: participate and group follow it,
// everything else stays with the person
ra_current = ra_rows.map((d, i) => ({
  ...d,
  participate: ra_assign[i],
  group: ra_assign[i] === 1 ? "participant" : "comparison"
}))

ra_vars = Object.keys(ra_data).filter(v => !["participate", "group"].includes(v))
```

<!-- means table, with the full data beside it (styles in style_9.css) -->
::: {.ra-tables}
```{ojs}
// means of each variable by group
ra_mean = (v, p) => d3.mean(ra_current.filter(d => d.participate === p), d => d[v])

// how each variable's mean is shown (the 0/1 variables as percentages)
ra_fmt = {
  const pct = v => `${Math.round(v * 100)}%`
  return {
    test_score: v => v.toFixed(0),
    income: v => `$${v.toFixed(0)}k`,
    age: v => v.toFixed(1),
    prek: pct,
    y0: v => v.toFixed(0)
  }
}

// name shown for each variable
ra_labels = ({
  test_score: "Base Test Score",
  income: "Fam Income",
  age: "Age",
  prek: "Did Pre-K",
  y0: "Y(0)"
})

// the y0 row is bold italic (styles in style_9.css)
html`<div class="ra-means"><table>
  <thead><tr><th>Variable</th><th>Participant</th><th>Comparison</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${ra_vars.map(v => html`<tr class=${v === "y0" ? "ra-y0" : null}>
    <td>${ra_labels[v]}</td><td>${ra_fmt[v](ra_mean(v, 1))}</td><td>${ra_fmt[v](ra_mean(v, 0))}</td>
  </tr>`)}</tbody>
</table></div>`
```

::: {.ra-full-wrap}
```{ojs}
// full data table, collapsed until the full data button is clicked.
// participate is left out to save space (group shows the same thing)
ra_full_cols = Object.keys(ra_data).filter(v => v !== "participate")

// built once each time it's opened; ra_full.update() then rewrites the
// cells in place when the data changes, rather than redrawing the table
// (which flickers and loses the scroll position)
ra_full = {
  if (!ra_show_full) return html``
  const fmt = x => typeof x === "number" && !Number.isInteger(x) ? x.toFixed(1) : x
  const rows = d3.range(ra_n).map(() => ra_full_cols.map(() => html`<td></td>`))
  const el = html`<div class="ra-full"><table>
    <thead><tr>${ra_full_cols.map(v => html`<th>${v}</th>`)}</tr></thead>
    <tbody>${rows.map(cells => html`<tr>${cells}</tr>`)}</tbody>
  </table></div>`
  el.update = data => data.forEach((d, i) => ra_full_cols.forEach((v, j) => {
    rows[i][j].textContent = fmt(d[v])
  }))
  return el
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
ra_full.update?.(ra_current)
```
